title: Parade work: marching with Paul Barbarin
summary: Purnell says he played only two days of parades, with Paul Barbarin's band, including Labor Day on Canal Street, and wanted no more.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Oh, what I wanted to ask you was, did you do any parade work? Any parade work?

Well, see, I was in the man so much around that, see, when you come to the parade, I played a parade. I played a parade. I played a walk in high. Once I played a parade. Twice, two days, I played. I played with Paul Barbarin. Boy, and then people walking from nine o'clock that morning to six o'clock that evening. With the square deals. Man, no more parades. Then I played the Labor Day parade the next day. On Canal Street. I played from the river and Canal Street to Elf's Place. And that was all. Who's band was that? Paul Barbarin.
I used to play him, too. But that was enough parade work.
